Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1b) demonstrates bilateral widening of the lower posterior mediastinum with smooth, lateral displacement of both paraspinal lines (indicated by arrowheads) and no evidence of vertebral destruction or respiratory symptoms. This radiographic pattern is characteristic of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma involving the posterior mediastinum, distinguishing it from neurogenic tumors (typically unilateral), abscesses (associated with infection/vertebral changes), or extramedullary hematopoiesis (usually associated with severe anemia and rib notching).
